channel.title: Nature Materials
channel.description: Nature Materials is a multidisciplinary journal aimed at bringing together cutting-edge research across the entire spectrum of materials science and technology. Nature Materials covers all applied and fundamental aspects of the synthesis/processing, structure/composition, properties and performance of materials. Nature Materials provides a forum for the development of a common identity among materials scientists while encouraging researchers to cross established subdisciplinary lines. To achieve this, Nature Materials takes an interdisciplinary, integrated and balanced approach to all areas of materials research while fostering the exchange of ideas between scientists involved in different communities.

item.title: [8] Excitons driving spin dynamics in CrSBr
item.content:encoded:
Last authors: Wenyi Zhou, Roland K. Kawakami

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Experimental study of spin dynamics in 2D antiferromagnet; relevant to magnetic quantum materials.

Tags: #experiment #2Dmaterial #antiferromagnet #spindynamics

Abstract: Photoexcited excitons in the two-dimensional antiferromagnet CrSBr are found to act as a source of spin torque, driving nonlinear magnon dynamics through phase-coherent energy exchange that persists well beyond the optical pulse.

item.title: [8] Microwave-to-optical transduction using magnon–exciton coupling
item.content:encoded:
Last authors: Andrea Alú, Vinod M. Menon

Authors: Pratap Chandra Adak, Iris E. McDaniel, Suvodeep Paul, et al.

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Experimental study of magnon coupling in a layered antiferromagnet, relevant to quantum materials.

Tags: #experiment #2Dmaterial #antiferromagnet #magnon #quantuminformation

Abstract: Broadband microwave-to-optical conversion is demonstrated in the layered antiferromagnet CrSBr through strong magnon–exciton coupling, offering a scalable platform for quantum transduction.
